name: Selection cycling through overlapping entities on repeated clicks
body: Clicking again on the same spot selects the next entity under the cursor, front to back, so an entity hidden behind another can be selected without hiding the front one.
plan:
- The session keeps the pixel of the last plain click and the keys it has selected there, front to back.
- On a plain click's release (no Shift or Command, no drag), if the click lands within the click slop of that pixel and the selection is still just the last key, it picks the nearest entity under the cursor that it hasn't visited yet. With none left it starts again from the front.
- Any other click, a drag, or a selection made some other way starts a new cycle.
- Presses are unchanged, so pressing and dragging still moves the entity under the cursor.
- The status line says which entity it reached and its place in the stack, for example "Selected pillar_2 (2 of 3 under the cursor)".
- Tests go in tests/editor, through the session: three overlapping entities, repeated clicks, the wrap, and a reset when the pointer moves.

acceptance_criteria.text: Repeated clicks on one spot step front to back through the entities under it, then wrap
A click elsewhere, a Shift-click or a drag starts over from the front
